operative_sections_inspected.quote: ER/PM raise a Design Change Request (DCR) against a TRSO version. Impact is mapped to affected modules, triaged and priced via the rate card (Section 4).
Module delta price and tooling/validation delta; "include / exclude / swap" flag; priced as options at RFQ

Locked rate card: machine-hour rates, labour, overhead and profit %, scrap norms and raw-material index formulae are agreed at S3 and held for the nomination period. A change re-uses them, so only quantity, weight, cycle time or new-part inputs are re-quoted.

operative_sections_inspected.section: Exception clauses — target calibration and safety override
operative_sections_inspected.quote: A change that touches safety-critical content is Class C by default unless Quality records a documented override.

operative_sections_inspected.section: Exception or provisional clauses — provisional authorisation
operative_sections_inspected.quote: Provisional authorisation: where the design is stable enough, Purchase may issue a capped, time-limited Letter of Authority so the supplier starts development/tooling while pricing closes. Cap and expiry set by Finance; it lapses automatically.
Change bundling: small changes raised within a set window are bundled into one pricing and approval round instead of one per change. Safety-critical items are never held back for bundling.
Delegation of authority: Class A/B approvals can be delegated by role and by value band, with an automatic substitute when an approver is absent.
Escalation, not deemed approval: if an approver does not act within the SLA, the item escalates to their superior; silence is not treated as approval for Finance or Quality.

Zero-cost changes: changes with no cost impact (e.g. a finish change with no cost-driver movement and no safety or homologation content) are recorded with a zero-delta confirmation and no re-negotiation.

Governance retained: no change is effective without a revised, signed Nomination Baseline; PM sees every open DCR and its timeline impact; Finance retains authority over price and Quality over safety content.
Versioned objects: TRSO, Module, Supplier, RFQ/Quote, Negotiation round, Nomination Baseline, DCR, Approval, Document.
Configurable stage and gate definitions, class-based routing, parallel approvals, SLA clocks, escalation, delegation and substitutes, all changeable by admin without code.
Module tree with cost-driver templates; rate card and index formulae; automatic roll-up; delta versus baseline; option activation; supplier portal for quote entry and confirmation.
Immutable, timestamped log of communication trails, negotiation summaries, evaluations and legally valid e-signatures (replacing physical signatures); full retrospective search and export.
Systems of record to be confirmed with TechSol.
Role dashboards for PM, Finance, Quality, ER and Purchase: open DCRs, ageing against SLA, schedule impact, price delta; notifications on every gate.
Role-based access, supplier data segregation (a supplier sees only its own quotes), availability and retention as per company policy, mobile approval. Tech stack is left to TechSol.
Phase 2: modular quotation engine, rate cards and class-based routing, piloted on one headlamp and one tail lamp programme.

Success measures (targets to be set after Phase 1 baseline): change-cycle time per class, share of changes closed as Class A/B, number of full re-negotiations, approvals past SLA, and project-timeline slip attributable to design changes (today: up to 50%).

Only one artifact was supplied; no companion files or sheets were available for inspection. The 2–3-page requirement remains unverified because rendering was not performed; that is not treated as a demonstrated page-count failure.
